Print a Model Term

Source: R/generics.R
print.model_term.Rd

Prints one line naming the term's class, its label when it has one, and whether it is built. A built term reports how many coefficients its block carries; a specification says so and names the call that would build it. This is the default for every term class, and several classes override it to add what they alone carry.

Arguments

x

A term, built or not.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches print()'s.

Value

x, invisibly. Called for the line it writes.

Details

The two forms are

<SmoothTerm> 's(x)' built: 4 coefficients
<SmoothTerm> 's(x)' (specification; call term_build() with data)

The class name is the S7 class's own, the label comes from the label property and is omitted when empty, and the count is ncol(x@X).

A structural term has no X to count, so it gets the word built and no count. Every shipped structural term registers a method of its own, so this line is reached only by a structural class written outside the package.

The classes that override this add something of their own: print.PenalizedTerm() names the penalty and the standardization, gas()'s and regime()'s report their parameters, nl()'s its formula and seg()'s its break-points.

See also

term_is_built() for the predicate it branches on, term_coef_names() for the names behind the count.

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:4)

# A specification, and the same term built.
linpar(~ x)
#> <LinparTerm> (specification; call term_build() with data)
term_build(linpar(~ x), d)
#> <LinparTerm> built: 2 coefficients

# The label is shown when there is one.
s(x, k = 5)
#> <SmoothTerm> 's(x)' (specification; call term_build() with data)
linpar(~ x, label = "lin")
#> <LinparTerm> 'lin' (specification; call term_build() with data)
